editorial:
Imagine the most awkward live TV show you have ever seen, then multiply it by ten. That is exactly what you get here. You follow Nick and Kelly, two news anchors who are just trying to keep their jobs while hosting a disaster of a holiday fundraiser. The vibe is pure chaos from the start. Between a weather guy who only cares about his own hair and a station owner who is completely out of touch, the whole event feels like a train wreck that you cannot look away from. It is the kind of movie that makes you laugh because everything is going so wrong.

The acting is great because the cast really leans into the absurdity of the situation. The pacing stays quick, so you never feel bored, though some of the jokes are a bit silly. If you love cringe comedy, you will have a blast. To get the best experience, you should definitely stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to catch all the funny facial expressions. If you are a movie collector, grabbing the 4K Blu-ray is a smart move for your physical library. It is a perfect pick for a lazy Christmas Eve night with friends.
endingExplained: The show ends in total disaster, but the chaos actually makes the broadcast go viral. Because people love watching train wrecks, a huge wave of donations pours in from across the country. The network is saved from bankruptcy not because of the talent, but because the show was so bad it became a hit. Nick and Kelly finally bond over the madness, and Jon Sampson gets a reality check about his ego.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves awkward humor and holiday movies.
